races.name: Dino Family Day At Fairyhouse Optional Claiming Race

runners_data.name: Henry Hudson
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for David Marnane who has handled Good ground adequately (sim-going 2/3) but has not won or placed on it; Luke McAteer takes the ride and the 1m2f trip is a step up that could suit, though the slow expected tempo may blunt any late challenge.
runners_data.comment: Henry Hudson has shown a clear upward curve across his last three starts, progressing from seventh to fourth with a fair speed figure of 58. He's yet to win in that time, though, and a 28-day break raises a slight fitness question.

runners_data.name: Mare Crisium
runners_data.note: W J Lee partners this unexposed filly for K J Condon; all form to date is on Soft or Heavy, making today's Good to Firm her first genuine test on quick ground — that going concern is the key unknown, but her unrated style (U) means she could press forward and shape a race few others want to lead.
runners_data.comment: Mare Crisium has finished mid-pack in each of her last three starts, without a win in that time, though she does have experience at today's trip. A modest speed figure of 61 keeps expectations in check.

runners_data.name: Pass The Buck
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's colt carries experience over further (17f, 10f) and has placed twice in six similar-going runs; his true hold-up style is a liability in a slow-run sprint, but the step back to 1m2f from staying trips could unlock a sharper response if things set up better than expected.
runners_data.comment: Pass The Buck tops these figures at 63, a recent third and fourth marking a step forward from a rougher patch before that. Experience at today's trip could bring further gains, though he remains without a win in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Arizona Star
runners_data.note: Peter McCreery's filly shows a tendency to fade late and her historical record on similar going (2/5, 0 wins, 0 places) offers little encouragement; shifted into midfield on the map as a genuine hold-up type crowded out at the rear, her STYLE_FIT flag of 0.90 tempers confidence that she'll produce her best running out of role.
runners_data.comment: Arizona Star's recent form reads modestly, with just one frame placing in her last five starts and without a win in that sequence, leaving her towards the bottom of these figures at 43. Experience at today's trip is about her only source of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Zitkala Sa
runners_data.note: Colin Keane — a key booking — rides this Kevin Coleman-trained filly who has three runs on Good ground and placed once (3rd); a natural come-from-behind operator, she has been pushed into midfield on the map because too many hold-up horses compete for the same ground, meaning Keane will need to improvise positionally.
runners_data.comment: Zitkala Sa rates second-highest in this field at 58, improving to third last time out with experience at today's trip already banked. The switch to first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces could unlock more, though she remains without a win in her last four starts.

runners_data.name: Borora Aura
runners_data.note: Ran just six days ago, which warrants monitoring for residual fatigue, though trainer Michael Mulvany has hit with 1/12 runners recently; Gary Carroll rides and this filly's best course form at 10f on Good gives her a legitimate profile for today's trip and ground, and her unrated style means she may drift forward in the absence of committed leaders.
runners_data.comment: Borora Aura boasts a strong speed figure of 76 and returns quickly, just 6 days after her latest run, with prior form at today's trip and ground. She's yet to win across her last six starts, and her form has swung between midfield and further back.

runners_data.name: Akissfromarose
runners_data.note: The headline OR of 120 is misleading — recent form reads 0-0-9-0 and she has faded to the rear in all four recent starts on soft and standard going; the switch to Good to Firm represents uncharted territory for Daniel Murphy's filly, and the "fades in finish" flag alongside the slow expected tempo makes a big run hard to construct.
runners_data.comment: Akissfromarose sits bottom of these figures at 31, with a run of well-beaten efforts and without a win across his last four starts. A recent outing 14 days ago at least keeps him ticking over, but there is little else here to recommend him.

runners_data.name: Tenacious
runners_data.note: Mrs John Harrington's runner has had 51 days off since last seen, a notable freshness angle that could cut either way; labelled a true hold-up horse mapped into midfield, Nathan Crosse will need to find a workable position early — the horse's single placing on similar going (3rd over 8f on Good) came when stepping back in trip, which is not happening today.
runners_data.comment: Tenacious rates third-highest in this field at 56, and a third-place effort in her recent form shows genuine ability on her day. She's without a win in her last five starts, though, and mostly modest form plus a 51-day break count against her.

runners_data.name: Music And Song
runners_data.note: Thomas Dowling's filly has four runs at today's 10f trip on Good or Soft, placing once (4th), but the "fades in finish" flag is a consistent concern; Rory Mulligan's 5lb claim provides a small compensating advantage, yet as another true hold-up type shifted into midfield, she needs a genuine pace that this field is unlikely to generate.
runners_data.comment: Music And Song's latest run, a fourth, was her best of the last six starts, though she remains without a win in that time. First-time cheekpieces and experience at today's trip offer some encouragement, but a modest speed figure of 55 tempers expectations.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in the field, this 1m2f contest on Good to Firm ground at Fairyhouse is set to be run at an uneven, drifting tempo with the majority of the nine runners preferring to race off the pace. Mare Crisium and Borora Aura carry unknown style (U) ratings and may press forward from the gates, but neither is a committed pace-setter, meaning the early fractions are likely to be pedestrian before the race ignites in the final two furlongs. The absence of a genuine lead horse creates a bunched, tactical affair that will almost certainly resolve into a sharp sprint finish from the home turn, favouring runners with tactical speed rather than pure staying ability. This race shape strongly suits horses who can sit prominent or mid-division and produce a decisive turn of foot in the closing stages — hold-up horses are penalised because the slow early pace will negate any late run. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear: Henry Hudson, Pass The Buck, Zitkala Sa, Tenacious, Arizona Star, and Music And Song all prefer to come from off the pace, but with so many sharing that profile only a handful will find clear daylight late — those who can adapt and sit closer to the pace will have a material advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the race drifts on a muddling gallop and resolves into a two-furlong dash from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Mare Crisium and Borora Aura, floating forward without genuine front-runners to confront them, set a false pace that compresses the field; the finish becomes a flat-out sprint where tactical speed and freshness matter most.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Mare Crisium or Borora Aura establish a clear lead early and control the tempo through the final bend.
scenarios.body: A genuine rhythm is set for the first time, denying hold-up horses any sweeping momentum late; the runner able to quicken off a controlled front sets a standard that stragglers cannot peg back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If an unexpectedly honest gallop is set and hold-up horses find clear ground entering the straight.
scenarios.body: Pass The Buck or Henry Hudson, sitting patiently in rear, benefit from a genuine pace and reel off their finishing effort; this scenario is discounted because several true hold-up types (Zitkala Sa, Tenacious, Music And Song) are racing out of their natural role and are unlikely to produce a clean late run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Produces Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If the lack of pace creates interference and positional scrimmaging that disadvantages the fancied hold-up types.
scenarios.body: An adaptable runner who can slot into a fluid mid-division and avoid traffic trouble finds the gaps first; Borora Aura's recent 6-day turnaround and course form on Good going makes it a candidate if the field bunches and then fragments.

watchPoints.text: Mare Crisium and Borora Aura are the only plausible pace-setters — if neither goes forward from the gates, the race could degenerate into a walk that renders all form figures meaningless.

Zitkala Sa carries the Colin Keane booking into a race where her natural hold-up style is compromised by field congestion — watch whether Keane opts to press forward rather than get caught in a mass of hold-up runners at the rear.

Akissfromarose's OR of 120 will attract market interest, but her last four finishes (all double-figure positions) and consistent fading pattern make the rating extremely stale — beware false favouritism.

Pass The Buck's trainer Joseph Patrick O'Brien has a strong recent record (9/56 in 14 days) and the colt has placed on similar going — minor place positions rather than win potential in this shape, but worth monitoring in each-way markets.

Borora Aura runs for the second time in six days; if she shows any signs of staleness in the paddock or early strides, her role as a potential pace-maker evaporates and the entire race shape becomes even more formless.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
Irish Stallion Farms EBF (C & G) Maiden
Fairyhouse Winter Festival 28th & 29th November Rated Race

runners_data.name: Royal Hollow
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old confirmed front-runner for Andrew Slattery, she has placed in 6 of 11 similar-going runs without a win in that sample, and the uncontested lead here is the key asset — though her STYLE_FIT tag suggests she is racing slightly outside her most effective role, tempering confidence in a win.|
runners_data.comment: Royal Hollow rates the best of this field at 85, with a win and two runner-up efforts among her last five starts showing real consistency. She already has experience at today's trip and carries 142lb here, with just one below-par run to spoil the sequence.

runners_data.name: Light Up The Dark
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's 5-year-old returns after 91 days off but arrives on the back of a win (1/13f/GOO) and has proven ability on good-ground variants; three wins from eight runs in similar conditions is a solid strike rate and the 1m6f trip suits his recent profile.|
runners_data.comment: Light Up The Dark won last time out, one of two victories in her last five starts, backed by a strong speed figure of 83 and experience at today's trip. The obvious concern is a 91-day absence since that win, leaving her fitness in question.

runners_data.name: Buddy One
runners_data.note: A 9-year-old hold-up specialist for Paul Gilligan who has not run in 298 days (119 jumps days), with his best efforts recorded at marathon trips of 20f-26f on heavy ground — the switch to a sharp 1m6f on Good to Firm is a significant concern, and the yard has sent out 0 winners from 5 runners in the past 14 days.|
runners_data.comment: Buddy One won two starts back, showing he has the class for this level, and already has experience over today's trip plus a rating of 82. An unplaced effort last time and patchy form around that win are the obvious worry.

runners_data.name: Tounsivator
runners_data.note: Mullins and Keane is a formidable combination, and this prominent-runner won at 12f on good ground but has been off 269 days; his last three outings over 16-17f on good ground produced two single-figure finishes, suggesting the trip is within range — fitness from such a long break is the only genuine question.|
runners_data.comment: Tounsivator won three starts back and carries a strong speed figure of 81 to match, rating 81 himself in this field. His runs either side of that win were much weaker, though, and a 269-day absence raises real doubts over his fitness.

runners_data.name: Sir Callisto
runners_data.note: Has won two of his last four at 12f on standard AW and arrives in form, but all his recent efforts are over 12f on artificial surfaces — this step up to 1m6f on turf is an unexplored combination, and while he is a natural front-runner, there are simply too many prominent types ahead of him in the queue for him to secure his preferred berth.|
runners_data.comment: Sir Callisto's form has been mixed, sandwiching a win and a runner-up effort between finishes further back, including a below-par latest run. A modest speed figure of 62 tempers the upside, though the ability shown in between keeps him on the fringes of this.

runners_data.name: Chutzpal
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's 7-year-old carries a hood and has placed four times in 12 similar-going runs including a win, but his last run was a well-beaten 24th in a 14f good-ground race; naturally a prominent racer by trade, he finds himself squeezed out of that position in this field's shape, which blunts his tactical edge.|
runners_data.comment: Chutzpal sits low in these figures at 72 despite a fine run of form that included a win and three frame finishes, backed by a strong speed figure of 86. His latest effort was blank, though, and first-time blinkers arrive off a 45-day break.

runners_data.name: Not Just Any Eagle
runners_data.note: A 7-year-old hold-up type for a small yard (0/9 in T14) ridden by a 7lb claimer — his last five runs show five finishes of 7th or worse including a run-out, and while Good to Firm is not a stated concern, his form profile offers very little to recommend at this level.|
runners_data.comment: Not Just Any Eagle has failed to reach the frame in any of his last five starts, without a win in that time, though he does have experience at today's trip and going. A fair speed figure of 78 hints at more than the results suggest.

runners_data.name: Pavilion End
runners_data.note: Trained by Charles O'Brien, this 6-year-old's actual profile is that of a hold-up horse, though the surplus of closers in the field means he sits in a redistributed midfield position; his last five starts include five double-figure finishes (worst: 13th twice) on good and standard, and he has no visible route back into contention from here.|
runners_data.comment: Pavilion End sits bottom of these figures at 72, his form having faded from an early third to back-to-back unplaced efforts without a win in that time. Experience at today's trip and a fair speed figure of 76 are about the only positives to cling to.

races.paceDynamic: Royal Hollow is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no serious challenger for the lead, will dictate an uncontested, sustainable gallop over this 1m6f trip on Good to Firm ground at Fairyhouse. Light Up The Dark and Tounsivator will track from a prominent position, with the latter returning from a lengthy 269-day absence for Mullins and Keane. The field actually contains more prominent-minded types than the map can accommodate — Sir Callisto, Chutzpal, and Pavilion End are all genuine prominent or hold-up horses who are likely to find themselves racing out of their natural position, with Royal Hollow and Light Up The Dark most likely to physically secure the front two berths. A controlled pace set by Royal Hollow strongly favours horses who can travel economically close to the pace and pick up off a steady gallop — prominent racers with a clean passage and a turn of foot are the primary beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Royal Hollow Dictates Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Hollow sets a controlled, uncontested pace and the field settles without challenge, the race is run entirely to her agenda.
scenarios.body: Royal Hollow bowls along at a measured gallop, and horses who track her closely — particularly Light Up The Dark and Tounsivator — are perfectly positioned to challenge in the straight; the lack of early pressure means stamina is not truly tested and a clean break from the prominent box wins.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Close Trackers Sweep Past
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Hollow's pace is modest enough that the prominent stalkers sweep past her in the final two furlongs with fresh reserves.
scenarios.body: Light Up The Dark, who showed a win last time at 14f on soft and has placed on good ground, has the class and profile to hit the front off a slow burn; Tounsivator, back from a long absence but trained by Mullins with Keane aboard, could prove a dangerous second string if fit enough.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow and the front-runners stop suddenly in the straight, allowing a closer to swoop from the rear.
scenarios.body: Buddy One, whose best efforts have come at longer trips, or Not Just Any Eagle could theoretically pick up late ground, but both have poor recent form and the good-to-firm ground is a concern for horses who need a stamina-sapping race to come into play.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Traffic Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the surplus of prominent-minded types — Sir Callisto, Chutzpal — push forward and force a faster-than-expected pace that destabilises the race shape.
scenarios.body: With Sir Callisto and Chutzpal both naturally wanting to race up with the pace but mapped into midfield, any surge for position could quicken the tempo and catch Royal Hollow cold, opening the door for a horse with tactical versatility; Sir Callisto is on a hat-trick at this level but is stepping up significantly in trip.

watchPoints.text: Royal Hollow is the only natural front-runner in the field — if she is taken on early by Sir Callisto or Chutzpal pushing forward from their unnatural midfield positions, the tempo could spike and undermine the controlled pace shape the whole race is built around.

Tounsivator returns after 269 days off for Mullins and Keane, and a forward move from the tracking position cannot be ruled out — an absence-fit watch on how sharply he travels in the early furlongs will indicate whether he arrives race-ready or needing the run.

Sir Callisto steps up significantly in trip to 1m6f on turf having won exclusively at 12f on artificial surfaces — watch whether he travels with his usual fluency or struggles for oxygen from halfway, as the combination of trip, surface, and lost positional berth stacks up against him.

Buddy One has not raced under rules for 298 days and runs for a yard with no winners from their last five runners — check for market moves; any significant support for a horse this lightly tried in this context would be a meaningful signal.

Light Up The Dark's 91-day break is the only flag against what is otherwise a compelling profile — watch his pre-race behaviour and how sharply J M Sheridan positions him in the first furlong; if he settles kindly in second or third, the race is set up ideally for him.

races.name: Darley Irish EBF Stanerra Stakes (Fillies' & Mares' Group 3)

runners_data.name: Floresta
runners_data.note: Won twice at Group level over 1m4f-1m6f on Good ground and has a genuine prominent racing style that suits tracking Goodie Two Shoes here; 64 days off is a potential query but J P Murtagh's yard is 3/22 over 14 days showing decent recent form, and cheekpieces add a focus angle.
runners_data.comment: Floresta won twice in her last five starts but finished unplaced last time out following a 64-day break. She does have solid form at today's trip, though, and a rating of 95 keeps her firmly in contention rather than out of it.

runners_data.name: Galileo Dame
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's mare has a win and a place at Leopardstown over 1m6f+ on Heavier ground, but seven-of-fifteen on similar going is a concern; naturally a front-runner by inclination, she will likely find herself further back than ideal given the congested pace picture and that positional compromise tempers expectations.
runners_data.comment: Galileo Dame rates 104 here, boosted by a strong speed figure and prior form at today's trip and ground. She's yet to score in her last five starts, though, and a below-par seventh 22 days ago is the main concern.

runners_data.name: Goodie Two Shoes
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed front-runner, she has four wins over 1m4f-1m6f including two on Good ground, and this role is entirely natural for her — on a flat course with no one to challenge her from the gates she is the key tactical asset in the race and the horse around whom everything else is planned.
runners_data.comment: Goodie Two Shoes strung together two wins before a below-par eighth last time out, and she rates top of this field at 107. First-time tongue-tie could sharpen her up further, with experience at today's trip already banked.

runners_data.name: Jannah Star
runners_data.note: O'Brien's four-year-old has modest form figures of 3-4-4-6-8 and no wins at this level; naturally inclined to race up with the pace but pushed back into a midfield role by the crowded prominent tier, she is asked to operate out of character and her flat recent form on Good ground (8th, 6th) gives little encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Jannah Star's form has faded across her last five starts, sliding to an eighth last time out and yet to win in that sequence. She does have experience at today's trip, but a rating of 87 leaves her towards the bottom of this field.

runners_data.name: Nuit
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the ride for De Bromhead on a mare whose best form — a 2nd at The Curragh over 1m2f on Standard and a 3rd over 1m4f on Good — came when prominent; she is a genuine front-running type shunted into midfield by the race shape, and 64 days off adds a fitness query on top of the positional challenge.
runners_data.comment: Nuit has been a model of consistency with frame finishes in four of her last five starts, though she's yet to win in that time and returns from a 64-day break. First-time tongue-tie and prior form at today's trip are in her favour.

runners_data.name: Perfect Your Craft
runners_data.note: Pat Twomey's charge won over 1m4f on Good at Gowran and was second over 1m2f on Good at The Curragh, showing clear affinity for these conditions; Willie Lee rides from a natural tracking position and 1m6f is the key question — she hasn't yet won beyond 1m4f but has the engine to try.
runners_data.comment: Perfect Your Craft won four starts back and carries a strong speed figure of 90, rating 98 to sit third-highest in this field. First-time cheekpieces add interest, but a below-par fifth last time out is the obvious blot on her claims.

runners_data.name: Bloom
runners_data.note: Aidan O'Brien's three-year-old carries a 13lb weight-for-age allowance versus the older horses and her Good-ground form is solid (1W3P from five runs); she races prominently and Wayne Lordan should get a handy berth, but 1m6f is new territory for a filly who hasn't yet run beyond 1m4f.
runners_data.comment: Bloom won four starts back and followed up with two solid thirds, backed by a useful speed figure of 89 and past form on today's ground. Her main concern is a below-par seventh last time out, breaking that promising sequence.

runners_data.name: Dreamkeeper
runners_data.note: Noel Meade's three-year-old won over 1m4f on Good at Roscommon just eight days ago — the quick turnaround and step up to Group 3 company are both significant asks; naturally an up-with-the-pace runner but mapped further back due to the crowded prominent tier, and her Timeform figures don't yet match this level.
runners_data.comment: Dreamkeeper sits bottom of these figures at 78 — she won two starts back but could only manage sixth last time. A rapid 8-day reappearance is about the only other thing in her favour on this form.

runners_data.name: Ice Dancer
runners_data.note: The only genuine hold-up horse in the race, Ronan Whelan will need either a strong pace or a gap to materialise in the straight, and neither looks likely given Goodie Two Shoes's expected control; her Good-ground form reads 7-7-9 from her last three, and she hasn't won beyond 1m (8f) in her career.
runners_data.comment: Ice Dancer's form has faded sharply since a win earlier in this sequence, slumping to ninth last time out and sitting second-bottom in these figures. First-time blinkers are the one change that could yet arrest the decline.

races.paceDynamic: Goodie Two Shoes is the lone confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner Group 3 and, with no genuine rival to press her from the front, she should be able to control the gallop from the outset over 1m6f on Good to Firm ground at Fairyhouse. The pace is therefore expected to be honest but sustainable — a steadily-run affair that keeps the race together for longer than a truly contested lead, making it harder for hold-up horses to find the gap they need in the straight. Floresta, Perfect Your Craft and Bloom are the natural prominent trackers who can sit just off the leader and pounce, while the genuine hold-up type Ice Dancer will need things to go wrong up front to get involved. The field contains more front-running and prominent types than can all occupy their natural positions — Nuit, Galileo Dame, Jannah Star and Dreamkeeper are true prominent racers redistributed to midfield because the shape simply cannot accommodate them all, meaning they are likely to race out of role. **This race shape strongly favours horses who can track the controlled pace from a prominent position and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs, not those who need a truly strong gallop to close into.**

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Goodie Two Shoes Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Goodie Two Shoes leads uncontested and sets a comfortable, well-judged gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: She dictates from the front, avoids any pace war, and quickens up the straight having conserved energy — her Good going form (two wins) underlines she handles these conditions well.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse sits just off Goodie Two Shoes's measured pace and outstays her in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Floresta or Perfect Your Craft, racing in a genuine tracking role at 1m6f on Good to Firm, use the steady gallop to get a perfect tow into the straight and wear down the leader; both have recent form over this trip and going combination.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Closers Arrive
scenarios.trigger: If the pace hotts up in the middle stages — perhaps Nuit or Galileo Dame push forward — turning it into a true stamina test.
scenarios.body: A stronger tempo would compress the field and theoretically open the door for Ice Dancer to close from behind, but her recent Good going form is poor (four nines and sevens in her last three) making this a low-confidence shape for her.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Springs Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If the race falls apart tactically with multiple horses jostling for prominent positions and the pace becomes fragmented.
scenarios.body: Dreamkeeper, fresh from a win 8 days ago and lightly raced, or Jannah Star could sneak through if chaos disrupts the front-runners' rhythm, though both are racing out of their natural prominent role here and face a stiff OR task.

watchPoints.text: Goodie Two Shoes — watch whether J M Sheridan settles her in a true rhythm in the first half-mile; if she is harried by Nuit or Galileo Dame forcing their way forward, the race dynamic shifts entirely and her advantage evaporates.

Nuit and Galileo Dame — both natural prominent types, they risk getting into a quiet war for position behind the leader in the early stages that wastes energy and makes life harder for both; watch the first two furlongs to see who secures the better berth.

Bloom — carrying a 3-year-old weight allowance, watch whether Wayne Lordan elects to slot in behind the leader or gets shuffled back; if she gets a clean run into the straight at 1m6f the age allowance could prove crucial in a slowly-run race.

Ice Dancer — the one confirmed hold-up horse, watch whether she gets any cover or runs into an early traffic problem; in a controlled-pace race at 1m6f she will need horses to tie up in front of her, and Ronan Whelan will have to be patient almost to the point of risk.

Going — the official going report consistently reads Good to Firm across all distances at Fairyhouse today; Goodie Two Shoes and Floresta both have strong form at similar conditions, so watch for any late-going change announcement that might benefit those with softer-ground form like Nuit or Galileo Dame.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Maiden

runners_data.name: Banshof
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 4-year-old for Matthew J Smith with uncertain style; recent form of 6th and 8th at shorter trips on similar ground offers little encouragement, and the step up to 7f is untested territory with only two runs under the belt.

runners_data.name: Pettus Bridge
runners_data.note: Denise Foster-trained 4-year-old whose sole run produced 11th over 1m2f on Good, well beaten and flagged as prone to fading; drop to 7f is an unknown but the form reads poorly and McGettigan's claim doesn't add obvious class.

runners_data.name: Auguste Gusteau
runners_data.note: Cahill-trained 3-year-old who is a natural hold-up horse but the volume of closers in this field means he is unlikely to get into his preferred position at the rear; his best of 6th from three starts on similar ground suggests limited ability even when conditions suit.

runners_data.name: Bamako Beach
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes over on this M D O'Callaghan 3-year-old who has placed twice at this exact trip including a 2nd on Good, making him the confirmed pace-setter; flagged with STYLE_FIT as he maps to prominent when his natural profile is more pace-prominent, but an uncontested lead on Good to Firm is his best-case scenario.

runners_data.name: Chloe's Boy
runners_data.note: Rogers-trained 3-year-old who is a genuine hold-up horse but the crowded rear means he is being bumped forward on the map; his only run was a 14th of 15 over 8f on Good, and the fade flag combined with that bare form makes it hard to find an angle of appeal.

runners_data.name: Cladach
runners_data.note: Unraced Joseph Patrick O'Brien 3-year-old with unknown going preference and style; the trainer's volume and quality of maidens — 10 winners from 67 in the last 14 days — make debutants from this yard worth respecting, and Scott McCullagh gets the ride on what could be a well-prepared runner.

runners_data.name: Coolshine
runners_data.note: Heffernan-trained 3-year-old who fades late and has finished 9th and 11th from two runs on Good and Soft; hold-up style over distances longer than today's trip suggests this 7f assignment doesn't obviously help, and the recent 14-day return from a run looks routine rather than prep-sharpened.

runners_data.name: Farewell To Arms
runners_data.note: Charles O'Brien 3-year-old returning after 54 days with two modest runs on Good and Healy Park; the hold-up style and fade flag are a concern in what could be a steadily-run race, and finishing 8th and 13th from further trips doesn't inspire confidence at this level.

runners_data.name: Passage Of Power
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien 3-year-old returning from a significant 176-day absence with only a single 3rd-place run over 6f at the Curragh to his name; the unknown style rating and lengthy break are the two key questions, but the pedigree and trainer suggest the step to 7f on quick ground could unlock improvement.

runners_data.name: Shay's Dream
runners_data.note: O'Brien-trained 3-year-old with consecutive last-place finishes over 7f-8f on Good and Tapeta; fades late and is mapping to midfield, and there is little in the form or pace profile to suggest the race shape will rescue a horse with this record.

runners_data.name: Sindagan
runners_data.note: J P Murtagh's 3-year-old with Ben Coen booked, carrying real form credentials with four placed runs including a 2nd and two 3rds all over 7f in similar conditions; the prominent style suits this projected race shape ideally and the consistent placed record gives him the most transparent profile in the field.

runners_data.name: Storzando
runners_data.note: Debut runner for Michael Mulvany with Wesley Joyce's 3lb claim; no going, style or form data to assess, but Mulvany has sent out a winner from 12 recent runners and Joyce's light weight could be a factor if the horse shows natural ability on a flat, fast surface.

runners_data.name: Thumama Sands
runners_data.note: McGuinness 3-year-old who has finished 11th and 14th from two runs at this trip on Soft and Good; the fade flag, hold-up style, and modest form make it difficult to construct a scenario where the projected steady pace here helps rather than hinders.

runners_data.name: Goomah
runners_data.note: Lupini-trained 3-year-old whose best effort was a 3rd at 7f on Good — the most relevant piece of form for today — but as a natural hold-up horse being pushed into a midfield position by the volume of closers in the race, Lordan will need a different ride than ideal; the STYLE_FIT tag tempers confidence even if the raw form has some merit.

runners_data.name: Little Sure Shot
runners_data.note: De Bromhead's 3-year-old returning after 102 days with a blinker addition noted; has placed at 8f on Good and shown some ability, and W J Lee is a respected pilot, but as a true hold-up horse mapped to midfield in a race where the pace is expected to be steady, the conditions actively work against what the horse needs to produce its best.

races.paceDynamic: Bamako Beach is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 15-runner maiden, with Colin Keane booked to lead from stall and set what should be a sustainable, uncontested gallop on Good to Firm ground over 7 furlongs at Fairyhouse. With no genuine challenger for the lead, the pace is unlikely to be truly searching, which historically favours horses able to travel prominently and quicken off a steady tempo rather than those relying on a strong pace to close into. Sindagan and Passage Of Power are the principal prominent types capable of tracking Bamako Beach through the race, while debutants Cladach and Storzando add unknown quantities from the front half. The field holds significantly more hold-up horses than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Auguste Gusteau, Chloe's Boy, Goomah, and Little Sure Shot are all natural hold-up types redistributed to midfield on the map, meaning their true tactical roles will be compromised in a race where the pace is likely to be modest. This race shape firmly favours prominent racers who can track the front-runner, as a steady gallop will not generate the late pace deficit that genuine closers need to pounce.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Bamako Beach bowls along uncontested at a fair but undemanding clip and the race lacks any mid-race surge.
scenarios.body: Sindagan and Passage Of Power track the leader throughout and hit the rising ground with something in reserve, with Bamako Beach potentially staying on powerfully if the gallop has been conservative enough to allow it; a one-paced finish on Good to Firm suits horses who have been travelling with cover rather than expending energy from off the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Debutant Surprise Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unraced runners — Cladach or Storzando — shows sharp natural ability and quickens clear before the field can react.
scenarios.body: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's Cladach is particularly notable given the trainer's 10/67 recent strike rate and strong record with debutant maidens, and a well-schooled newcomer who travels prominently and picks up off a steady tempo could prove too good for more exposed rivals; Storzando for Michael Mulvany adds a second unknown quantity that could capitalise on a slowly-run affair.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Closes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest and a horse racing from deep finds clear running to finish strongly through the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Little Sure Shot showed a placed effort at 8f on Good and could stay on into a place if pace is strong enough, while Goomah's best effort of 3rd at 7f on Good shows some ability in similar conditions; however, both are redistributed from their natural hold-up positions and the steady pace predicted actively works against their profile, making this scenario the least reliable despite individual ability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Bamako Beach's recent 2nd-place efforts at this trip translate and Keane times a front-running ride to perfection on the good-to-firm surface.
scenarios.body: Bamako Beach has placed twice over 7f and shows course-appropriate form, and an uncontested lead at a pace that suits could see it simply stay on relentlessly without ever being caught; the discounted probability reflects the STYLE_FIT tag noting it is racing out of its most natural role and the field's depth at the prominent end.

watchPoints.text: Sindagan is the horse to watch most closely — Ben Coen rides a 3-year-old with four placed runs all at this exact trip, a prominent style that fits the projected race shape, and the form book behind him; if he travels smoothly off Bamako Beach's back this could be a dominant performance.

Cladach and Storzando are both unraced debutants from quality yards — O'Brien and Mulvany respectively — and either could prove significantly better than the exposed form in this field; watch the market move and the early price on both as a guide to stable confidence.

Bamako Beach's uncontested lead is only an advantage if Keane manages the pace correctly — if he dawdles excessively through the early stages, he risks gifting the prominent and midfield horses a short, sharp test that negates his lead; watch the early sectionals.

Little Sure Shot returns from 102 days off with blinkers, and De Bromhead's 5/22 14-day strike rate suggests the yard is in reasonable form; the headgear change and freshness angle are worth monitoring even if the race shape is not ideal for a hold-up horse.

The number of hold-up types redistributed to midfield — Auguste Gusteau, Chloe's Boy, Goomah, Little Sure Shot — means there could be significant scrimmaging for position in the early stages behind the lead, which may create trouble in running for horses drawn wide or slow away from the stalls.

races.name: Winter Festival Early Bird Tickets From 20 Euros Handicap

runners_data.name: Rahmi
runners_data.note: OR 102 top-weight hold-up horse with two wins and five placings in 15 similar-going starts; Ben Coen takes over for J P Murtagh's yard who show 2/29 in 14 days, and Rahmi's best form on good ground over this exact trip makes him the primary closer to track in Scenario A.
runners_data.comment: Rahmi heads our ratings and carries the highest official mark here, with a clear speed edge to match. Proven over today's trip, he returns from a 24-day break under top weight from stall one; recent placings have been modest since his sole win, the one blemish.

runners_data.name: Tolebi
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner returning quickly on 12 days' rest for a trainer who has gone 0/5 in the same window; three poor efforts in his last three starts and a sim-going record of 0 wins from 9 attempts makes him a difficult proposition despite the fitting style.
runners_data.comment: Tolebi holds the second-highest official mark here and sits second on our figures, having raced over today's trip before. He was fourth two starts back and is quick to return, but he's yet to score in his last five, finishing only ninth last time out.

runners_data.name: Bishopton
runners_data.note: Prominent racer in good recent form — a win and a second from his last five — for a trainer firing at 2/8 in 14 days; goes well on good ground over seven furlongs and is one of the few runners fully able to secure his natural position tracking Indigo Dream's lead.
runners_data.comment: Bishopton won four starts back and was runner-up the time before, useful form at this level. He arrives fresh off an 11-day break with both today's trip and going covered, though his placings have since faded to sixth last time, the one query.

runners_data.name: Exquisite Acclaim
runners_data.note: Second run back from a break, 12 days ago, and a genuine hold-up type by nature — though with more hold-up horses in this field than the rear of the race can accommodate, he may find himself racing slightly ahead of his ideal position; visor retained, and sim-going stats of 0 wins from 15 are difficult to ignore.
runners_data.comment: Exquisite Acclaim was runner-up before winning next time out, form that stands up well here, and he already has today's trip and going covered. His last four runs have been modest, no better than fourth, but a first-time visor could bring extra sharpness.

runners_data.name: Indigo Dream
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter for Ross O'Sullivan, wearing a tongue tie; her STYLE_FIT flag reflects that in a truly contested scenario she may not dictate as freely as her natural role demands, but with only modest pressure expected she should lead and set a manageable fractions on Good To Firm ground.
runners_data.comment: Indigo Dream has been freer with places than wins, third and twice runner-up earlier in this sequence, but her latest three read fourth, eighth and unplaced. She's yet to win in her last six starts, though she does have today's trip covered, a query still unanswered.

runners_data.name: Glory To Be
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with a solid recent profile including five placings from 15 similar-going runs and a tongue-tie in place; Wayne Lordan is a strong booking and the horse returns on just seven days' rest, suggesting the yard is confident — one of the few who can legitimately share prominent ground with Indigo Dream.
runners_data.comment: Glory To Be rediscovered form with a runner-up effort last time out and is quick to return, just seven days later. She has today's trip and going covered and wears cheekpieces for the first time, though a flat spell through seventh and ninth muddies the picture.

runners_data.name: I Bid You Ajou
runners_data.note: By nature a prominent racer but the field is too crowded up front for him to take that position freely — Gavin Ryan rides for a 0/11 trainer in 14 days, and while his recent Good ground form at six furlongs is consistent, stepping to seven and conceding position is a compounding concern.
runners_data.comment: I Bid You Ajou has been freer with places than a win, twice runner-up in this sequence yet still winless in his last six starts. A month off since his latest run is the obvious query, though today's trip and going are both already covered.

races.paceDynamic: Indigo Dream is the confirmed front runner and, with only Glory To Be and Bishopton as genuine prominent challengers, she is set to stride into an uncontested lead on a flat, fair Fairyhouse seven furlongs where the going report confirms Good To Firm conditions all evening. The pace will be sustainable rather than scorching — a single leader dictating her own rhythm with two rivals tracking at a respectful distance creates a controlled, even tempo that keeps the race honest without turning it into a sprint test. This shape favours hold-up horses who can travel through the race on the bridle and produce a clean, progressive run in the final two furlongs, particularly those who carry proven form on good ground over this trip. Notably, the field holds more prominent and hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate: I Bid You Ajou is a genuine prominent runner who is unlikely to secure that position against Indigo Dream, Bishopton, and Glory To Be, while Exquisite Acclaim is a true hold-up horse shuffled back further than ideal — closers who depend on these two racing in their natural role should temper expectations accordingly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Closers Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Indigo Dream leads at a steady Good To Firm gallop and the race develops into a test of finishing quality over the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Indigo Dream sets a measured pace with Bishopton and Glory To Be tracking closely, leaving genuine hold-up horses like Rahmi with a target to chase down on a flat track that rewards sustained finishing runs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Pair Battle, Hold-Up Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Glory To Be or Bishopton pushes hard for the lead early and forces a faster pace than Indigo Dream intended.
scenarios.body: Increased pressure on the front end uses up the prominently-placed runners in the final furlong, opening the door for a hold-up horse producing a single powerful late run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Duo Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Indigo Dream and Glory To Be stride clear of the field early and the hold-up horses find the gap too large to bridge late.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a two-horse battle up front with the closers spending their run closing ground rather than winning it, suiting the prominent types who travel economically in behind the leader.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Hold-Up Lands
scenarios.trigger: If Indigo Dream sets a falsely slow early pace before a sharp acceleration tests the hold-up horses' ability to quicken from an unfavourable position.
scenarios.body: This suits the highest-rated closer in the field but depends on horses like Rahmi overcoming a wide gap with limited time to close, making it the least likely shape given the flat track and honest posted going.

watchPoints.text: Indigo Dream must be monitored leaving the stalls — if she dwells or is slow away, the entire race shape collapses and the tactical verdict for closers shifts dramatically.

Glory To Be is five-from-five in the places on similar going and returns on just seven days' rest with a top-10 jockey; if she travels into the race comfortably she could prove stronger than her OR 79 suggests.
Rahmi's wide draw and hold-up style means any crowding or loss of momentum rounding the final bend could deny him a clear run — watch for Ben Coen's positioning at the two-furlong pole.

The going report confirms Good To Firm for this race despite the stated Good classification — horses with a strong record on faster ground, particularly Rahmi and Bishopton, may have an unquantified advantage over those whose best form came on softer surfaces.

I Bid You Ajou's last win came at six furlongs on Good ground and he has never won at seven — his redistribution to midfield combined with a distance query makes him a horse to watch for how Gavin Ryan deploys him rather than a win expectation.

races.name: Racing Again September 21st Handicap

runners_data.name: Faoladh
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner in the race and the key pace-setter; has won and placed twice at 7f on Good ground in recent form, though Andrew Slattery's yard is 2 from 24 in the last 14 days, and the STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence in its ability to fully replicate that dominant role if pressured late.
runners_data.comment: Faoladh won two starts back and was third the run before that, useful form in this company. He has today's trip and going covered and wears a tongue-tie for the first time, though he needs to bounce back from a below-form sixth last time out.

runners_data.name: Chester Nimitz
runners_data.note: Nicola Burns (5) takes the ride for a yard with no recent form (0/5 T14), but the horse won over 6f on Good ground and has prominent-running form that fits this scenario perfectly; 12 days since last run is fresh enough, though the step back from 8f to 7f could suit.
runners_data.comment: Chester Nimitz tops our ratings, his win four starts back the form that gives him claims to confirm that potential here. He already has today's trip covered and is quick to return, though a run of ninths in his last two starts is the query.

runners_data.name: Loingseoir
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old prominent racer trained by M C Grassick who has placed four times over 7f on Soft, and Good to Firm could be faster than ideal; Jack Cleary (5) takes over in the saddle and the yard has 1 win from 6 runners in the last 14 days, making this a live each-way contender at the pace.
runners_data.comment: Loingseoir has been improving, moving through ninth and seventh to back-to-back fourths in his last two starts. He's yet to win in that run and returns after a 27-day gap, though today's trip is covered and he sports a first-time tongue-tie.

runners_data.name: Shoot To Kill
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type (tagged hg:p) who placed at 2nd over 7f Good and 3rd over 8f Good recently, showing the form is there; 27 days since last run, and Noel C Kelly's yard is 1/5 in the T14 window — needs more pace than Faoladh is likely to generate.
runners_data.comment: Shoot To Kill was runner-up and third either side of his current slump, but a below-form eighth last time raises questions, and he's yet to win in his last five. Today's trip and going are both covered, and cheekpieces are added for the first time.

runners_data.name: Surpass And Shine
runners_data.note: Has been off the track for 334 days, which is a major flag regardless of earlier form over 5f on Good; Robyn Donaghue-Leahy (7) carries an apprentice claim but the trip (7f, longest run to date) and lengthy absence make this a very speculative runner.
runners_data.comment: Surpass And Shine has landed two wins in this spell, but they're sandwiched by well-beaten efforts and his last two starts were both unplaced. A 334-day absence since his latest run is the major concern, though today's trip and going are already proven.

runners_data.name: Imperial Dream
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose best recent form — a 2nd at 7f on Sta and 4th at 7f Sta — came on a surface that differs from tonight's Good to Firm; Alan Persse (5) rides and the yard is 0/8 over the last 14 days, suggesting limited stable confidence at present.
runners_data.comment: Imperial Dream sits second on our figures despite a modest official mark, the form built on a runner-up effort four starts back. He's yet to win in this run and his last two starts were both unplaced, though a 65-day break could bring improvement.

runners_data.name: Carrigans Grove
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for Patrick J Flynn who raced just 7 days ago and has placed four times at 6-7f on Good; blinkered (hg:p), which can sharpen focus, and Gary Carroll is a smart booking for a horse that wants to race close to the pace in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Carrigans Grove shaped up better three runs back when fourth having been eighth before that, but her last two starts were both unplaced, still without a win in her last five starts. A week's turnaround and a useful speed figure offer some encouragement, plus cheekpieces for the first time.

runners_data.name: Hugo's Girl
runners_data.note: W J Lee takes the mount on a filly with three places over 5-6f on Good, including a 2nd at 5f; she is a genuine hold-up type pushed to midfield on the map due to field congestion at the rear — her best form has come at shorter trips, and the 7f on Good to Firm may stretch her stamina.
runners_data.comment: Hugo's Girl has been a model of consistency, placed in four of her last five starts including a runner-up effort two starts back, the exception a below-form run in between. She's yet to win in this sequence, though a quick week's turnaround and today's trip covered count in her favour.

runners_data.name: Green Kite
runners_data.note: Colin Keane is a significant jockey booking, but Green Kite carries a finish-fade flag and has zero wins or places from three runs at 7f+ on Good going; a true hold-up horse repositioned to midfield on the map, and Kevin Coleman's yard has had 1 win from 9 in the last 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Green Kite's runner-up effort last time out was the pick of this sequence, a step up from a rockier spell of eighth and unplaced form before that. He's yet to win in his last five and sits 12th of 15 on our figures, hard to trust fully.

runners_data.name: Contrary To Law
runners_data.note: Unknown style (tagged U) trained by J P Murtagh, who has 2 wins from 22 runners in the last 14 days; Ben Coen aboard is a strong pilot and the horse has form over 7f Good (4th), though it has not won in four starts and the headgear flag suggests some behavioural question marks.
runners_data.comment: Contrary To Law's best run in this sequence was a fourth three starts back; his other efforts read seventh, sixth and, further back, ninth. He's yet to win in his last four starts and is over a month off that run, though today's trip is covered, plus a first-time hood.

runners_data.name: Unidos
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type with a finish-fade flag and zero wins from four starts; form includes a 5th over 6f Good which is its best recent effort, but 26 days off and Ronan Whelan aboard cannot mask that this horse has yet to show a winning move in this company.
runners_data.comment: Unidos has struggled for form in this sequence, no better than fifth and with two unplaced efforts among his last four starts. He's yet to win in that run and sits down at 13th of 15 on our figures, some way below his official mark, leaving plenty to prove after a 26-day break.

runners_data.name: Belle Nuit
runners_data.note: Two-year-old returning after 248 days off the track for Paul Nolan, who is 0/3 in the T14 window; the form figures of 540 were earned at 7f-8f on Soft/Heavy, and while Chris Hayes is a seasoned jockey, the layoff and Good to Firm ground combine to make this a risky proposition.
runners_data.comment: Belle Nuit progressed from fifth to fourth across her first two starts in this spell but found only an unplaced effort last time out. She's yet to win in her last three starts and is back from a lengthy 248-day absence, with today's trip already in the book working in her favour.

runners_data.name: Rappell
runners_data.note: Prominent runner (hg:b, blinkers) with form figures of 900906, meaning no place in recent outings over 6f on Good; J M Sheridan rides for a yard with no wins from 13 runners in the last 14 days, and this horse is struggling to show its earlier ability in current form.
runners_data.comment: Rappell has struggled for a big placing in this sequence, no better than sixth in his last six starts including two ninths. He's yet to win in that run, though a fair speed figure and a quick week's turnaround offer a sliver of hope, with blinkers added for the first time.

runners_data.name: Peig Sayers
runners_data.note: Has run 22nd over 8f on Heavy and consistently finishes in the bottom half of fields; a true hold-up horse placed at midfield due to field congestion, carrying a finish-fade flag, and the yard is 0/1 in the T14 window — hard to make a case for involvement at the business end.
runners_data.comment: Peig Sayers has finished unplaced in each of her last five starts, leaving little to work with on form alone. She's yet to win in that run and rates 14th of 15 on our figures, an official mark of 52 reflecting that. Today's trip already covered is about her only positive.

runners_data.name: Sonoma Sunset
runners_data.note: Off for 76 days and trained by W T Farrell, who has no recorded runs in the last 14-day window; a natural hold-up type pushed forward on the map with a finish-fade flag, and form figures of 6900-0 tell the story of a horse currently well out of form at 7-8f.
runners_data.comment: Sonoma Sunset props up our ratings in this field, with her last three starts all unplaced and only a ninth and sixth further back to speak of. She's yet to win in that sequence and returns from a 76-day break, leaving little in these figures to inspire confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Faoladh is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 15-runner field and, critically, faces no serious challenger for the lead — this horse will stride to the front uncontested and control tempo from the off on Good to Firm ground at Fairyhouse over 7f. With just one pace-setter dictating a sustainable, unforced gallop, the early fractions are unlikely to be punishing, which will suit horses travelling close to the pace rather than those needing a strongly-run race from off the pace. Several apparent hold-up types — Hugo's Girl, Green Kite, Peig Sayers, and Sonoma Sunset — are redistributed to midfield on the map because the field contains more genuine hold-up horses than can all settle at the rear in a race with this little pace; their true role is further back, and they are unlikely to get a truly strong gallop to chase down. The tactical verdict is clear: with a single uncontested leader setting a controlled pace, prominent racers who can sit just behind Faoladh and pounce in the final two furlongs hold the decisive structural advantage, while true hold-up horses face the double problem of a slow enough gallop to blunt their finishing effort and traffic through a large field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Faoladh Leads, Prominent Chase
scenarios.trigger: If Faoladh controls tempo unchallenged and the race is run at a measured, even gallop throughout.
scenarios.body: Faoladh dictates from the front on Good to Firm ground and is never asked a serious question until the 2f marker, giving horses positioned just behind a clean sightline into the straight; Chester Nimitz, Loingseoir, and Carrigans Grove are all prominent types well-placed to pounce as the pace naturally increases.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Type Swamps Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow in the early stages and a prominent racer kicks before the final furlong and catches Faoladh flat-footed.
scenarios.body: A measured gallop set by Faoladh suits horses that can produce one decisive burst from just off the pace rather than a sustained grind; Shoot To Kill, despite a hold-up tag, has placed on Good ground at 7f and could get close enough at the top of the straight to challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Finishes Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens significantly in the straight and several prominent types crowd each other, opening a gap for a horse finishing from mid-division.
scenarios.body: Hugo's Girl has the form to run into a place at 5-6f on Good ground and could thread through late if the rail opens, while Contrary To Law with Ben Coen aboard has placed at 7f Good before and represents a stable that can time a handicap run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is surprisingly honest and true hold-up types get the strong pace they need to close from the rear.
scenarios.body: This is a low-probability shape because the field contains only one front-runner and the pace is expected to be controlled, making a deep-closing finish structurally unlikely; Green Kite and Sonoma Sunset are the most naturally suited profiles for this shape but both carry finish-fade flags and are poorly positioned for it.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Chester Nimitz can slot in directly behind Faoladh in the first furlong — if Nicola Burns (5) secures that position off a clean draw, the horse is ideally placed for a race that will be run at this pace shape.

Green Kite with Colin Keane is a market-mover to track; if Keane pushes forward aggressively to overcome the hold-up tag and take a midfield position, it changes the dynamics of who gets cover in the straight.

Hugo's Girl has W J Lee aboard and short recent form — if the field bunches in the straight as expected at this pace, she needs a clean passage and 7f on Good to Firm may expose her stamina limit at this distance.

Carrigans Grove races with blinkers and ran only 7 days ago; watch Gary Carroll for any sign of forcing tactics, which would be a tactical surprise in what is currently a single-paced race scenario but could disrupt Faoladh's rhythm early.

Surpass And Shine (334 days off, step up to 7f) is a horse to monitor in the market — if heavily backed despite the layoff, it may indicate stable confidence from Patrick J Flynn that the fitness concern is already resolved.
